Use case: identity-preserve. Production game animation IN-BETWEEN atlas. The input is an exact numbered-by-position atlas of existing key poses. Preserve every row's detailed original character, face, body proportions, clothing, hair, textures, props, mounts and facing direction. Do not simplify or redesign, no enlarged chibi heads. Create exactly FOUR COLUMNS and 13 ROWS of NEW intermediate animation frames. Within EACH ROW: output column1 is a new pose halfway between input columns1 and2; output column2 halfway between input2 and3; output column3 halfway between input3 and4; output column4 halfway between input4 and1 to complete the loop. These are newly drawn intermediate limb/motion poses, not copies, crossfades, ghost images or blurry morphs. Each output row belongs to the same input row. Walking: natural heel/toe transitions and arm swings; running: bent elbows, clear airborne stride transitions; mounted activities: rider stays seated, mount motion remains smooth; fishing/casting: rods and hands move gradually; other actions preserve their supplied sequence and costume. Feet/body anchors and visual scale stay stable; move only the parts that animate. Every frame in a directional row must keep the given facing, especially back-left (up-left, NOT up-right). For the one-row turn/call actions only, preserve their gradual changing heading as supplied. Row identities top to bottom:
